title: A learned feature increased sawtooth-lead use in generated music
summary: Researchers used a sparse autoencoder to find a feature associated with a sawtooth synthesizer lead in the text2midi model. Increasing the feature produced that instrument on 14 of 20 prompts, compared with 1 of 20 using a random direction. A second set of ten prompts showed a similar effect.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§4–5, prespecified confirmation and Table 5, held-out matched random direction, dictionary recurrence and limitations

evidence.tested: The prespecified confirmation compared the feature edit with a matched random edit and unmodified generation. The second test used disjoint prompts and a different seed.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns one feature in one selected model and an instrument represented explicitly in its MIDI vocabulary. It does not establish control of arbitrary musical attributes.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted sparse autoencoder discovers a feature in text2midi, whose decoded direction is directly varied on paired prompts to test instrument control.
